stage: immutable source-first inventory before fresh owner comparisons
priorExposure: Preceding vaccine/data and antigen audits exist; this inventory is not claimed blind to earlier project work.

rows.requirement: Keep the exact peptide and HLA protein attached to recognition claims; typing or a shared allele-group name alone does not prove tumour recognition.
Read the fictional two-copy report at HLA-A, HLA-B and HLA-C, retaining all six named alleles rather than treating the report as a unique personal barcode.
Distinguish locus, allele group, protein field, synonymous and noncoding fields and the N null-expression suffix; retain report resolution and ambiguity.
HLA-C*07:01 and HLA-C*07:02 share a first field but identify different proteins; transfer of a peptide or receptor result needs evidence.
Laboratory typing tests or sequences specified regions; Sanger and next-generation methods differ in coverage and phase-resolving ability by protocol.
Phase assigns differences to an inherited copy; compare tested loci and regions, resolution and alternative assignments before accepting the allele report.

Computational inference from genome, exome or RNA data retains dataset, software/version and validation; capture, coverage and expression limit it, and research inference is distinct from clinically accepted typing and peptide-display measurement.
Classical HLA-A/B/C commonly display intracellular-source peptides on most nucleated cells to conventional CD8 cells.
HLA-DR/DP/DQ class II mainly occurs on professional presenting cells with inducible expression elsewhere and is conventionally read by CD4 cells.
Class-I groove geometry is closed at both ends; scope the roughly 8 to 10 residue usual range and reported roughly 11-residue repertoire to the source rather than an absolute length rule.
Class-II groove is open at both ends and accommodates the cited roughly 13 to 25 residue range; datasets and individual peptides vary.
CD4 help and some cytotoxic CD4 responses do not demonstrate that a tumour displays the same peptide through class I.

Inherited type, tumour retention/expression, natural processing/display, matched recognition, function, safety and patient benefit are separate measurements; the diagram is a dependency chain rather than proof that every step occurred.
Proteasome cutting, TAP transport and ERAP trimming shape fragments; trimming can generate or destroy an epitope and more encoded windows do not bypass a shared processing defect.
B2M supports classical class-I structure, with shared loss effects across class-I targets distinct from class II; RNA alone does not establish assembled surface peptide-HLA.

Affinity estimates, eluted-ligand outputs and percentile ranks differ; retain allele, model/version and output, and 0.5 percent rank does not imply 99.5 percent benefit. Limited allele training warrants scrutiny rather than categorical exclusion.

In the fictional P example, A*02:01 prediction, A*24:02 receptor recognition and source RNA do not establish one naturally displayed recognised pair; seek matched-allele and controlled tumour-recognition evidence.

TNBC-MERIT presentation escape is one relapse specimen with downregulated processing genes including B2M and near-complete class-I protein loss; probable B2M downregulation is not a demonstrated new B2M DNA mutation or a recurrence/rescue rule.
Surface CAR recognition can avoid peptide-HLA restriction and NK responses depend on activating/inhibitory signals; neither becomes automatically effective after HLA loss.
The C*07:01 versus C*07:02 fictional prediction exercise needs the reported protein allele, resolution and model support; correct matching still leaves display, recognition and outcomes open.

Choosing a phase-ambiguous allele pair for favourable peptide predictions does not resolve inheritance; retain alternatives and obtain phase-resolving evidence, with later biological steps still unproved.
The display-stand analogy restates peptide-HLA compatibility.
Explain-it-back derives from the independent evidence stages.
Takeaway and next-step routing restate exact-pair evidence.
Citation list, source-check labels and pending expert/learner status are source metadata, not evidence credit.
Presentation, reagent binding, stimulated secretion and controlled target-cell effects answer different questions and do not independently establish clinical benefit.
Choose the experiment to reduce a named candidate-board uncertainty rather than to accumulate positive-looking results.
Immunopeptidomics identifies HLA-associated peptides in a specified preparation, leaving completeness, cell of origin, recognition and function open.
A specified peptide-HLA multimer labels sampled reagent-binding cells without by itself proving activation, natural tumour recognition or safe killing.
Peptide-stimulated ELISpot measures secretion-associated spots, not receptor identity or recognition of naturally presenting tumour cells.
A controlled tumour-cell assay supports effects under its defined conditions, leaving tissue safety, cell access, persistence and patient benefit open.
Compare sequence, allele, cell preparation, controls and analysis; complementary assays are not interchangeable and not every study uses all.
PBMC preparations mix circulating immune cells; processing and freezing affect recovery/responses and blood is distinct from tumour.
A multimer/flow percentage needs its parent population: T cells and all recovered cells are different denominators.
ELISpot interpretation retains input-cell denominator, background and positivity rules; prior culture expansion can alter the comparison.
ICS assigns a defined-stimulus cytokine response to gated stained populations; multiple cytokines do not establish target-cell death.
TCR sequencing supplies sampled receptor identities and clonality summarises their distribution; standard ICS and ELISpot do not supply receptor sequences.
Connecting a responsive population with a particular receptor needs a compatible identity experiment, rather than unrelated positive assay results.
A cytotoxicity assay requires target-only survival, effector-to-target ratio, incubation time and antigen/presentation controls; reduced growth or metabolism is not necessarily killing.
Synthetic peptide loading can supply abundant target while bypassing tumour production and processing; positive loaded-cell response needs a natural-presentation bridge.
The biological immunopeptidome has cell/HLA/time context; the identified list is an incompletely recovered subset.
Retain capture reagent, HLA class, sequence database and confidence criteria; computational allele assignment differs from directly isolating that allele.
Mixed tissue may supply cancer, immune or stromal peptides, and whole-cell extracts can recover intracellular HLA; detection does not prove tumour-cell surface display or tumour exclusivity.
Non-detection needs assay recovery and identification-sensitivity context rather than proof of biological absence.
A fixed paraffin block is not automatically a validated input for a named immunopeptidomics method; retain method-specific specimen requirements.

Barroso-Sousa 2020 compares 3969 primary/metastatic breast samples and receptor-defined subtype median TMB; higher group median in TNBC does not establish individual TMB-high classification, assay yield, display, treatment eligibility or benefit.
Receptor binding and cellular state/signalling differ; binding can label functionally different cells and a secretion assay can miss another response programme.
In the invented notebook, mixed-tissue peptide A detection requires identification confidence and cell-origin questions.
In the notebook, A-HLA blood multimer binding retains allele, staining controls and denominator, without a function conclusion.
More post-dose peptide-A spots require background, viability and expansion history, rather than unqualified natural tumour recognition.
A receptor sequence becoming relatively frequent does not identify the cells producing secretion spots or prove absolute expansion.
Keep the untested naturally presenting tumour-cell step visible despite several positives; a controlled positive strengthens that target/condition only, with safety and benefit separate.
Negative results can reflect sample quality, recovery or wrong reagent; positives can reflect background, loading or culture selection, so inspect controls.
Relative clone share can rise because other clones fall; longitudinal interpretation retains handling, absolute counts where available, method/version and analysis.
Non-detection by immunopeptidomics plus a strong loaded-peptide ELISpot response does not prove natural display; both biological and technical explanations remain.

Interpret the figure as independent HLA-peptide recovery, shared-scaffold multimer binding and incubation/capture followed by washed spot readout; shapes and spot counts are schematic, with no implied killing or patient benefit.

Source-check statements and citation list retain reading metadata without evidence credit.
Separate tumour event, longer encoded source window, processed epitope and the conventional TCR peptide-HLA target.
Several windows or pairs can arise from one event; ten windows are not ten independent alterations and multiple classical class-I alleles can share B2M dependence.
A stop-gain introduces termination rather than a new amino acid; unchanged upstream sequence alone supplies no new mutant peptide, while a frameshift can create an altered downstream tail.
In the fictional M/N comparison the unchanged truncated M label supplies no new sequence by itself, while N supplies a candidate tail; neither proves displayed recognition.
Nonsense-mediated decay depends on transcript context; retain mutant RNA support and later processing/recognition tests rather than use the prediction as a universal filter.
Credible tumour/normal sequence comparison supports an event without establishing expression or display.
Sampled mutant RNA does not alone prove protein production or processing.
Processing/binding prediction is model support rather than measured surface presentation.
Measured HLA-associated peptide supports the preparation with cell origin, recognition and safety still open.
A controlled T-cell response supports activity under the tested conditions without automatically proving natural tumour recognition or clinical benefit.
Controlled tumour-cell recognition or killing supports tested targets without establishing distribution, durability or benefit in patients.
A clinical outcome with a suitable comparison estimates benefit for that population, without automatic transfer to another product or setting.
Retain recovered-repertoire context and non-detection sensitivity, artificial loading limits and the exact tested method/version.
DAI compares predicted mutant and matching normal peptide-HLA binding with explicit formula/sign conventions.
DAI inherits prediction errors; a possible tolerance rationale is not a measured lack of tolerance or a validated universal selection rule.

Ghorani 2018 is retrospective advanced lung/melanoma cohort evidence, mean DAI associated with survival in three of five cohorts for clonal peptides, not measured display/recognition or prospective vaccine benefit.

Fictional K at 0.4 percent eluted-ligand rank and L at predicted IC50 40 nM are not numerically comparable; retain output/task, units, allele and version, and IC50 is not automatically an equilibrium binding constant.
Fictional A/B share Event 1 and allele X; B may add a window without independent coverage and loss of X challenges both.
Fictional C has measured HLA-associated peptide but unresolved cancer-cell origin and recognition.
Fictional D has peptide-stimulated response and needs natural tumour-recognition evidence.
Fictional E combines broad estimated tumour-cell fraction with weak RNA support.
Fictional F has RNA/prediction agreement but possible small-subclone coverage.
Fictional G is a class-II helper route needing presenting-cell/context evidence; it is not an established rescue.
Fictional H needs specificity work against similar healthy sequences; tumour-specific sequence does not prove selective recognition.
Fictional I has a strong rank with limited predictor support for its allele.
Fictional J has controlled tumour recognition but unresolved healthy-tissue specificity and durability.

Choose a next experiment against a named uncertainty rather than a universal A-J rank; for D a controlled tumour positive connects those tested cells, while a negative prompts processing/display/state/adequacy checks and neither estimates patient benefit.
Tumour-cell fraction and truncality inference depend on purity, copy number and altered-copy count; high raw variant read fraction does not prove a truncal target.
Correlated windows and model agreement are not independent validation; weighted models need appropriate held-out evaluation and explicit healthy-sequence/allele-support limits.
Class-I and class-II choices can support different response components without guaranteeing recognition or resolving a shared presentation failure.
Immunodominance may concentrate responses in a few encoded targets rather than all selected sequences.
Epitope spreading can extend observed recognition to unencoded targets but does not itself demonstrate clinical benefit.
Record selection and exclusion reasons, model versions, manual overrides and construct version as traceable design decisions.
Ten added windows from one alteration restricted to one lost allele increase count without repairing shared display dependence.

Under the fictional changed reports, X loss challenges A/B/C/J, whereas B2M-supported classical class-I failure challenges A-F and H-J; G needs separate class-II assessment and original open questions and clinical-ranking limits remain.
Original-only explanatory definition distinguishes the peptide HLA-contacting agretope from the TCR-reading face; retain it as an explanatory model rather than a universal structural partition.
